headline: US stocks fell as the 10-year yield hit a 19-year high and Brent hovered near $108 ahead of Fed rate decision
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) closed at 7,581 (-0.51%), the Dow ($DJI) at 52,069 (-0.67%), while the Nasdaq ($COMP) fell 0.8% and the Russell 2000 (IWM) lost 1.09%, marking a second straight decline for US equities.
- The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.04%, its highest level since 2007, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended recent bond-market actions amid the move.
- Brent crude (@QA) traded near/above $108 per barrel on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline shutdown and attacks, Strait of Hormuz risks, and broader Middle East supply tensions.
- Energy was the only S&P 500 ($SPX) sector to finish higher, up roughly 1.9%, while consumer discretionary underperformed, dragged by Dave & Buster’s (PLAY) 17% drop after missing Q2 revenue estimates.
- Dave & Buster’s (PLAY) shares tumbled 17% after the company reported Q2 revenue below expectations.
- AI-related chip names advanced as Intel (INTC) traded flat, Qualcomm (QCOM) gained 4%, AMD (AMD) added 2.3%, and Nvidia (NVDA) and Micron Technology (MU) also climbed on positive developments including Micron’s new memory validation, Intel (INTC)’s Altera IPO filing, and Nvidia (NVDA) AI partnerships.
- Financials weakened as Goldman Sachs (GS) fell 2.9% while JPMorgan Chase (JPM) rose 1%, with mixed moves amid higher borrowing costs from rising yields.
- Crypto-related stocks Coinbase Global (COIN) and Robinhood Markets (HOOD) declined after the Senate moved to block a key cryptocurrency bill.
- Ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve decision, markets priced in roughly a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike, which would be the first increase in three years under Chair Kevin Warsh, with attention on the rate decision, dot plot, and Warsh’s commentary.
- In after-hours trading, Trip.com Group (TCOM) reported earnings with no immediate stock reaction exceeding 2%.
